chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Suleyman ibn Khalid who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who initiates (a killing), so he attacks and gets counter-attacked, so there is no retaliation (qasas) for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on retaliation if the victim attacks first and is killed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'al-mubtadi' zalam' (the aggressor is wronged), establishing that if a victim initiates hostilities and is killed in the ensuing conflict, the killer is exempt from qasas (retaliation) because the victim's initial aggression forfeits their right to equal retribution. This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding self-defense and homicide, distinguishing between intentional murder and killing during a mutual altercation where the victim started the fight. It underscores the legal nuance that the right to life is not absolute when one actively breaches the peace through aggression.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Suleyman Bin Khalid who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying; ‘The one who initiates (a killing), so he attacks and get counter-attacked, so there is no retaliation for him’.
